pr_title: Add service block to formula api
pr_body:
- [x] Have you followed the guidelines in our [Contributing](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) document?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pulls) for the same change?
- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [x] Have you written new tests for your changes? [Here's an example](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/HEAD/Library/Homebrew/test/PATH_spec.rb).
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew style` with your changes locally?
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew typecheck` with your changes locally?
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew tests` with your changes locally?

-----

This fixes #14925.

The idea here is to include the service block info in the formula API JSON so that it can be loaded from the API. This will allow us to more consistently build service files and will mean that `brew services` doesn't have to be updated to work with the new API.

The first thing that was added was the ability to serialize and deserialize service blocks. We needed the ability to replace all local paths with placeholders when building the API JSON and then replace those placeholders with local paths when loading from the API.

The second thing was adding this service block JSON to the API and loading it from the API.

The other commits are just tests.

comments:
I talked with @carlocab and @Bo98 about this in #14952 and we think that the best way to solve this is to add the service block info to the formula JSON representation that we return from the API. This will require the least possible changes to `brew services` which makes the most sense. It will also fix a few other install from API related issues that it's having right now.

One important point though is that we will still need to substitute the HOME directory path when building the API JSON and then loading from it. We already do [something similar](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/1ff98350b2a6e208d24d427cb70a2b561c6491fe/Library/Homebrew/cask/cask_loader.rb#L317-L353) when loading casks from the API.

Another thing is that service files should not be included when bottling since we won't be using them going forward.
Does that also work for projects that ship their own plist/service file?

> Does that also work for projects that ship their own plist/service file?

Wait, there are bottles that ship their own plist/service files to the brew services file paths but that don't have service blocks in the formula source? And then they control them with `brew services`?

It seemed like that wasn't 100% supported right now when I looked earlier today and that's part of the reason I closed the above PR.

The idea I had was to remove generated service files from bottles assuming we'd rather include that info in the API JSON and generate them locally.

We could probably just leave them in the bottle if it's a problem since that's what we've done in the past. Basically, they would just get overwritten during install if a service block exists.
Yeah, if you check for "plist" in core you will find some that do. And generally it would fit our approach of "using upstreams defaults" to do this.

`brew services` doesn't properly support that but we could add DSL for that, e.g.

```rb
service do
  provided true
end
```

This will give the option to add `require_root` etc. like we could before with `plist_options`.

I was only able to find one instance of a service file being generated by hand in a formula and placed at one of the brew service file paths.

```
/u/l/H/L/T/h/homebrew-core (master|✔) $ git grep -A 4 -E 'homebrew\..*\.(plist|service)'
Formula/isc-dhcp.rb:    (prefix/"homebrew.mxcl.dhcpd6.plist").write plist_dhcpd6
Formula/isc-dhcp.rb:    (prefix/"homebrew.mxcl.dhcpd6.plist").chmod 0644
```

The `ice cream` formula does something similar but it doesn't end up at the expected file path so it wouldn't get covered by this.

Are there any other ones that I'm missing here?

All of the other ones used the `service do` block or the `def plist` method which are both supported when installing service files. The `def plist` method is not fully supported by `brew services` right now since it doesn't have a service block but I think it's a sort of legacy option. Anyway it's only used in 5 formulas.

```
/u/l/H/L/T/h/homebrew-core (master|✔) [1]$ git grep -E 'def plist$'
Formula/cassandra@2.1.rb:  def plist
Formula/cassandra@2.2.rb:  def plist
Formula/elasticsearch.rb:  def plist
Formula/elasticsearch@6.rb:  def plist
Formula/kibana.rb:  def plist
```

Either way we should probably just leave the service files in the bottle to get overwritten which is the current behavior.
I think there's also some that override `plist_name`.

> I talked with @carlocab and @Bo98 about this in #14952 and we think that the best way to solve this is to add the service block info to the formula JSON representation that we return from the API.

Could we use the `post_install` approach and use the formula from the bottle here instead?

> Either way we should probably just leave the service files in the bottle to get overwritten which is the current behavior.

Agreed.

> Could we use the `post_install` approach and use the formula from the bottle here instead?

We could but there's one notable difference to note here: the formula file for post_install only needs to be valid at install time while the formula file for a service needs to be valid ideally forever (or at least the lifetime of that package version).

Notably: if we deprecate something and change a postinstall then we can just rebottle. If we deprecate something and change the service block we would need to revision bump and hope people haven't done `brew pin`, and provide different deprecation messaging (it's currently aimed at maintainers).

We've had several problems in the past with deprecations and casks.
We could even plant this information in the bottle manifest, though maybe that's complicating things too much. Just showing how there's a few options here.
Cool, good explanation, thanks @Bo98, agreed given that the API makes the most sense here then.
Alternative option: we could also require all services to run in a working directory that brew controls. I'm not sure for any of the affected formula why it should be running in `$HOME`.

> Alternative option: we could also require all services to run in a working directory that brew controls.

I think this is really reasonable and probably makes this all a lot easier, right?
The problem doesn't exist in that scenario so yeah... that's a lot easier 😄

> Alternative option: we could also require all services to run in a working directory that brew controls.

Even if we did that we'd still have to substitute the home directory in the run command which shows up twice in `homebrew/core`. It also wouldn't solve the issues with `brew services` expecting a service block and not functioning as expected without it.

This might already be covered in the `brew services` problems that @Bo98 outlined above, but just in case it isn't, `caveats` for `service` blocks are currently not shown correctly when you don't have `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API` set. For example:

(That extra blank line bugs me to no end too. 😅)

@carlocab It looks like caveats are hardcoded when loaded from the API right now and that's what's probably causing the problem. Probably worth making a separate issue about that.

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/5550aa215e172f492cbcc137d64e79c57cb784c9/Library/Homebrew/formulary.rb#L266-L270

This is probably something we should look into addressing globally instead of case-by-case as issues come up. For casks, we already have a degree of this with `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` and `appdir`. Probably worth looking into adding that for formulae as well.

@Rylan12 I'm not sure we need such a generic solution for formulae. Right now this seems to only be needed for services and caveats. It's an interesting idea though.

> This is probably something we should look into addressing globally instead of case-by-case as issues come up. For casks, we already have a degree of this with `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` and `appdir`. Probably worth looking into adding that for formulae as well.

I agree, personally. Given this only applies to JSON generation: it feels a bit weird to have to do this in multiple sides that are going to end up in the same string in the end and can all be replaced there en-masse.
